newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans, Swiss connect in regional phone deal.
newsitem.headline: Germans, Swiss connect in regional phone deal.

text.p: Telecommunications monopoly Swiss Telecom PTT and two regional German utilities on Tuesday outlined plans for a cross-border venture that will create a new local challenger for Deutsche Telekom AG.

The new company, to be called Communications Network Services (CNS), will offer a broad spectrum of telecommunications services to businesses and later to residential customers in Baden-Wuerttemberg state.
Swiss Telecom will hold 50 percent of CNS and a holding company owned by utilities Energie-Versorgung Schwaben AG (EVS) and Badenwerk AG will hold the remaining shares.
The two utilities are in the process of agreeing a merger that will be effective retroactively to January 1, 1998 and will set the stage for later privatisation.
Baden-Wuerttemberg state owns 10.4 percent of EVS and 50.1 percent of Badenwerk. The remaining shares in both companies are held by municipal authorities.

Swiss Telecom and its German partners plan to invest a total of 300 million marks ($185 million) over the next five years to link their telecoms networks and set up a range services in competition to Deutsche Telekom.

Michael Gassner, head of Badenwerk's telecommunications activities said the new company expected to break even by the year 2002 and to become the second most important operator in the state next to Deutsche Telekom.
CNS has applied for and expects to receive soon a Class 3 operators licence to own and operate communications networks and a Class 4 licence to offer public phone services from the German government.
Beginning in July CNS will offer data services such as managed bandwidth services, X.25, frame relay and LAN interconnection as well as voice telephone services for closed user groups.
From 1998, when European telecommunications markets are open to full competition, the company plans to offer comprehensive telecommunications services to businesses and the public at large.
-- William Boston, Stuttgart newsroom, +49 711 6197355 ($ = 1.621 German Marks)
